title: Alert Orchestration Timeline and Escalation Affordances
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a compact, scrollable alert orchestration timeline that surfaces escalation affordances, on-call handoff snapshots, and one-click postmortem links in the Redwood Console. The goal is to reduce cognitive load during incidents, make escalation choreography explicit, and provide contextual links to runbooks and postmortems while preserving SLO surface area and cost signals.
acceptance_criteria: Timeline exposes chronological alert events with inline actions (ack, snooze, escalate) and shows SLO delta at event boundaries
Handoff snapshot component renders current on-call, last ack, and top 3 related runbooks with a single-click copy link
Postmortem quicklink flow opens a modal pre-populated with incident metadata and a suggested postmortem template link
Escalation affordance UI supports multi-step policies and shows estimated cost impact when using higher-capacity fallbacks
Figma prototype has accessible keyboard navigation and meets color-contrast for critical states
comments: 2026-03-09 - Kickoff: Reviewed scope with PM (Jonas Meyer). Decided to prioritize compact timeline + handoff snapshot over a full incident timeline to limit scope to 2 sprints.

2026-03-10 - Early sketch review: Eng raised a concern about high-cardinality tags in the timeline (alerts from multiple services). Proposed solution: collapsible group headers and sampling of noisy alerts.
2026-03-11 - Accessibility review: Added keyboard-first flows and explicit focus styles for inline actions. Color contrast updated for warning/critical states.
2026-03-12 - Design critique: PM asked for cost signals next to escalation steps. We added a micro-UI that surfaces estimated token/gpu cost and a confidence band for fallback behaviors.
2026-03-13 - Design -> Eng handoff: Created Figma prototype and attached implementation notes. Eng estimates 5 points for frontend + 3 points for backend event-surfacing APIs.
2026-03-14 - UX writing pass: Microcopy for 'escalate' clarified to 'escalate to higher capacity (may increase cost)'. Added rationale for modal confirmations on expensive fallbacks.

2026-03-15 - In Review: Design PR opened (link in attachments). Waiting on ENG-12034 for event enrichment and PM sign-off on cost microcopy. Planning a usability session with two on-call engineers next week.
next_steps: Run remote usability session with 2 SREs and 1 customer-facing support engineer (scheduled 2026-03-18)
Coordinate with ENG to add short-lived event sampling API to avoid timeline overload
Update prototype with live SLO delta visualizations and cost-estimate microcopy after PM approval
Prepare QA checklist for keyboard navigation and screen-reader labeling
notes_for_engineering: Backend must expose a condensed event stream: {timestamp, level, service, event_summary, runbook_ids, related_incident_id}
Provide an opt-in 'expanded mode' for high-noise services (togglable per-team)
Escalation fallback must return estimated token/gpu units used for a 60s window to compute cost heuristics
